Both briefs direct the fire ladders to extend and stop at the 7th floor.
Correction: The FDNY's longest 1911 ladder reached only the 6th floor — three storeys below the trapped workers on the 9th.
Source: Cornell ILR Kheel Center; FDNY demonstration

Problem: Shepherd is shown typing his famous account on a typewriter in a house den.
Correction: Shepherd phoned his account in live from the scene while the fire burned; Roy Howard took the dictation and telegraphed it out.

Problem: A lit cigarette sits in an ashtray beside a woman's sewing machine, with a rack focus onto it.
Correction: Smoking was banned inside Triangle and done concealed by male cutters; the Fire Marshal attributed ignition to a hidden match or cigarette dropped into a scrap bin under a cutting table.

Problem: Both records are filed under TSF but their creative direction is 'INT. RESTAURANT, NIGHT' and points artists at CCS_Stampede01/02.
Correction: These are another story's briefs mis-filed into the Triangle sequence — remove or re-slug before they go out as Asch Building shots.

Shotcodes: CTD_AI_TSF_InspectorOnPhone A; CTD_AI_TSF_InspectorOnPhone B; CTD_AI_TSF_BlanckLooksAtFactory A; CTD_AI_TSF_BlanckLooksAtFactory C
Problem: A fire inspector telephones Blanck and Harris in June 1909 to arrange a safety meeting, and Blanck hangs up.
Correction: The documented pre-fire approaches were written, unanswered correspondence about fire drills, not a telephone call.
Source: Cornell ILR Kheel Center; trial record

Shotcodes: CTD_AI_TSF_FireEscapeCollapse A; CTD_AI_TSF_FireEscapeCollapse C; CTD_AI_TSF_FireEscapeCollapse D
Problem: The fire escape is framed against 'EXT. ASCH BUILDING' with a birds-eye fall straight to the street.
Correction: The single fire escape was in the enclosed rear courtyard and terminated over a second-floor skylight, not on the public street facade.

Shotcodes: CTD_AI_ORA_PortholeSmashed; CTD_AI_ORA_ControlPanelDamaged A; CTD_AI_ORA_ControlPanelDamaged B; CTD_AI_ORA_ControlPanelDamaged C; CTD_AI_ORA_CrewAtControlPanel A; CTD_AI_ORA_CrewAtControlPanel B; CTD_AI_ORA_CrewAtControlPanel C
Problem: The whole broken-porthole and damaged-ballast-panel sequence is slugged INT. BALLAST CONTROL ROOM — DAY.
Correction: The portlight broke and water reached the panel between roughly 19:00 and 21:00 on 14 February, hours after a ~17:20 winter sunset — it must be night, as sibling briefs already specify.
Source: Royal Commission on the Ocean Ranger Marine Disaster, 1984

Problem: Men in the water without survival suits is slugged EXT. NORTH ATLANTIC — DAY while every other brief in the sequence is NIGHT.
Correction: The crew abandoned the rig from about 01:30 and were in the sea until it sank around 03:10 on 15 February — full darkness.

Problem: Briefs are built to sell the expert line that the rig is 'the length of two football fields'.
Correction: Ocean Ranger was 396 ft long and 262 ft wide — barely more than one football field. The '35 storeys high' figure is correct.

Problem: The liferaft canister is specified as 2.5 m long and 0.1 m high.
Correction: 0.1 m is physically impossible — a small offshore canister is roughly 0.5–0.6 m in diameter and moulded GRP, not white metal.

Problem: The lifeboat-inventory shots are specified as a 'sunny, warm winter day' with calm seas on the Grand Banks in February 1982.
Correction: 'Warm' will push the generator to summer light — specify cold, low, hard winter light over a calm sea to match the other February exteriors.

Problem: Three ECUs of the altimeter read 30,400 ft at the moment the captain requests a higher level.
Correction: KE007 was cruising at FL330 when it requested FL350, and was at 35,000 ft when the missile hit — 30,400 ft matches neither.

Problem: The slugline reads 'EXT. KAL007 (727)', which will cue a Boeing 727 nose.
Correction: KAL 007 was a Boeing 747-230B (HL7442) — the wide-body nose specified everywhere else in the story.

Problem: The aircraft is directed to nose-dive from cruise straight into the sea.
Correction: After the detonation KE007 arced upward for about 113 seconds, descended gradually, levelled at 16,424 ft for roughly five minutes, then spiralled down — about 12 minutes of flight.

Problem: The impact shot specifies 'rough waters' while the debris shot moments later specifies a 'calm ocean surface'.
Correction: Pick one sea state for the Moneron Island impact and carry it across both shots.

Problem: The deck crew is shown shovelling and levelling black asphalt with an asphalt roller in the foreground.
Correction: The 1 August 2007 job was concrete resurfacing — milling 2 in of concrete wearing course and placing a new 2 in concrete overlay, with aggregate piles, cement and water tankers and a concrete mixer on the deck.

Problem: Jeff Ringate is placed on the riverbank, fishing Lindsay Walz out from the shore.
Correction: Ringate was a construction worker who fell with the bridge; he spotted Walz from the collapsed deck and pulled her up onto it with a broom handle.

Problem: The beat states hundreds of vehicles plunge 110 ft into the Mississippi.
Correction: 111 vehicles were on the collapsed portion and only 17 were recovered from the water; the main span fell 108 ft into a river 15 ft deep.

Problem: A mid-1990s inspector hammer-taps visibly corroding gusset plates, framed as the discovery that mattered.
Correction: NTSB found the cause was under-thickness U10 gusset plates — a 1960s design error, not corrosion; corrosion at L11 was expressly excluded as causal.

Problem: Ringate is locked in as a recurring on-screen character described as a 'tall, blonde, Caucasian 20-year-old'.
Correction: No published account gives his age or appearance — confirm before building a recognisable likeness of a named living person across multiple shots.

Problem: Ignition is staged as an exposed cable wire on the mine floor throwing a spark into built-up methane.
Correction: MSHA determined lightning was the most likely ignition source and that the explosion occurred inside the sealed 2 North Mains area, where no cables or working faces existed.
Source: MSHA Report of Investigation, Sago Mine, 2007

Problem: Supervisors stand outside in overcast winter DAY at the 6:26 am explosion, and the escaping crew exits into DAY at about 7:30 am.
Correction: Sunrise at Sago on 2 January 2006 was about 7:40 am EST — the explosion happened in full darkness and the crew surfaced in dim pre-sunrise twilight.
Source: MSHA, 2007; NOAA solar position, Upshur County WV

Problem: Miners gear up with 'oxygen masks' around their necks, and underground one is taken off and put back on.
Correction: Sago miners carried belt-worn CSE SR-100 self-rescuers — single-use chemical-oxygen canisters that cannot be doffed and re-donned once started.

Problem: A miner drills the coal face with a hand-held jackhammer and roof bolts are driven with a sledgehammer.
Correction: Each Sago section worked with two remote-controlled continuous mining machines and two twin-boom roof-bolting machines — no hand drilling or hammered bolts.

Shotcodes: CTD_AI_SMI_JonesRalliesTeam; CTD_AI_SMI_BandanaOverMouth A; CTD_AI_SMI_SmokyTunnel; CTD_AI_SMI_EmergencyPhone A
Problem: Multiple briefs specify a mine ceiling around 6 ft with miners moving crouched.
Correction: Average mining height at Sago was approximately 7 ft — the men could walk upright.

Problem: Two versions of the same establishing sequence are dated 'Grey, Autumn Day 2005' and 'Grey, Autumn Day 2006'.
Correction: Fix one date — the disaster is early January, so autumn 2006 post-dates the event it is establishing.

Problem: Both briefs direct red-hot lava flowing down the side of the mountain.
Correction: No lava was produced in AD 79 — it was a Plinian pumice fall followed by pyroclastic density currents, so the mountainside carries ash and glowing surges, never lava streams.
Source: Sigurdsson et al., The Eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79

Problem: Pre-eruption Pompeii shots call for 'dormant Mt. Vesuvius' in the background, which will generate today's familiar cone.
Correction: The modern Gran Cono post-dates AD 79; in 62–79 AD Vesuvius was a single, taller, vine-covered summit inside a pre-existing caldera rim, and its top was destroyed in the eruption.

Problem: The pyroclastic surge that kills the Pompeians is slugged EXT. POMPEII — NIGHT.
Correction: The surge arrived about 07:30 on the morning of the second day — the blackness is ash-cloud darkness, so light it as daylight extinguished rather than a night scene.

Problem: The shot populates Pompeii's streets with Roman soldiers alongside villagers.
Correction: Pompeii was a civilian colonia with no standing garrison — confirm before dressing legionaries into an everyday street scene.

Problem: The 'just after flooding moment' version, in which a house is torn from its foundations, is slugged DAY in overcast daylight.
Correction: In Altenahr the house that broke loose went at about 21:50 on 14 July, after a ~21:30 sunset, and the flood peaked around 23:00 in full darkness.

Problem: The Sermanns' escape upstairs is slugged DUSK, yet the following brief shows the sun setting only after they are already up there.
Correction: Lukas Sermann and his father were cut off at about 19:00 on 14 July — broad overcast daylight in mid-July Germany — so the escape is a daylight scene and the dusk time-lapse follows it.

Problem: Lukas and his father shoulder open a door and scramble up flooded wooden stairs onto a balcony.
Correction: The published reconstruction has them stranded in the current and breaking into an ice cream shop for shelter — confirm the balcony detail.

Problem: The beat states seven people drowned at the campsite in Dorsel.
Correction: Regional records for Campingplatz Stahlhütte give six deaths; the site flooded around 16:00 on 14 July, which does support the DAY slug.

Problem: The same stretch of the Ahr is specified as 9 m wide in one brief and 12 m wide in the others.
Correction: Fix a single channel width so the pre-flood and flood-moment shots cut together.

Problem: The Altenahr riverbank explainer is specified as a sunny, cloudless day with sun sparkling on the water.
Correction: Every other Ahr brief is locked to overcast grey with rain or mist — a cloudless plate will not cut into the sequence.
